quests.question: The bridge is believed _____ built in the twelfth century.
quests.explanation: For an event that happened before the time of the belief, we use the perfect passive infinitive. The building took place in the past, so we need "to have been" + past participle.

quests.question: He had no idea that the decision _____ change his career for ever.
quests.explanation: "Would" expresses the future seen from a point in the past, here the moment before the decision. The main verb "had" is past, so "will" cannot be used.

quests.question: The employees were made _____ extra hours without pay.
quests.explanation: After "make" in the active voice, the infinitive has no "to", but in the passive it returns. So "they made us work" becomes "we were made to work".

quests.question: The company has three offices, two _____ are in Asia.
quests.explanation: "Of which" links a part to the whole group that has just been mentioned. It is used after quantities such as two, some or most.

quests.question: If only I _____ listened to your advice!
quests.explanation: "If only" + past perfect expresses regret about the past. The speaker wishes that a different action had happened.

quests.question: She looked at me _____ she had seen a ghost.
quests.explanation: "As though" introduces a comparison with an imaginary situation. It is followed by a past tense for something unreal.

quests.question: He chose to resign _____ accept the demotion.
quests.explanation: "Rather than" connects two alternatives that follow the same structure and shows which one was chosen. "Instead" would need "of" to work in this place.

quests.question: Nobody _____ the manager had a key to the storeroom.
quests.explanation: "Other than" means except and excludes the manager from the group. The other options compare quantities or alternatives.

quests.question: _____ the tight budget, the team did an impressive job.
quests.explanation: "Given" works like a preposition, meaning "considering". It introduces a circumstance that makes the result more remarkable.

quests.question: The fee is the same _____ of how many guests attend.
quests.explanation: "Regardless of" means that something does not depend on a factor. "Regarding" means about and would not fit.

quests.question: Please keep me _____ of any changes to the schedule.
quests.explanation: "Keep someone informed" uses the past participle as an adjective. It means to give updates regularly.

quests.question: We are committed _____ reducing our carbon footprint.
quests.explanation: In "be committed to", the word "to" is a preposition and is followed by an -ing form. It is used in company statements about their aims.

quests.question: She was promoted _____ senior analyst after only two years.
quests.explanation: We are promoted "to" a higher position. The preposition shows the new level that has been reached.

quests.question: He resigned _____ his post as director last week.
quests.explanation: "Resign from" is used for leaving a position or a job. The verb can also be used without "from" but not with the other prepositions.

quests.question: The contract is valid _____ two years from the date of signing.
quests.explanation: "Valid for" is followed by a length of time. "Since" refers to a starting point in the past.

quests.question: Employees are entitled _____ four weeks' paid holiday per year.
quests.explanation: "Be entitled to" means to have a legal right to something. The noun phrase after it names the right.

quests.question: We cannot share these details _____ the client's written consent.
quests.explanation: "Without" is a preposition and is followed by a noun phrase. "Unless" would need a full clause, such as "unless the client agrees".

quests.question: Payment is due _____ thirty days of receiving the invoice.
quests.explanation: "Within" shows the maximum time allowed, so the payment can be made at any moment up to thirty days. "During" does not express a time limit.

quests.question: The new results are consistent _____ our earlier findings.
quests.explanation: The adjective "consistent" is followed by "with". The phrase shows that two sets of results agree.

quests.question: The deal fell _____ because we couldn't agree on a price.
quests.explanation: "Fall through" is a phrasal verb for a plan or an agreement that fails to happen. The other particles do not form this meaning.

quests.question: We must work harder to keep up _____ our competitors.
quests.explanation: "Keep up with" means to stay at the same level as others who are progressing. Without "with", the phrasal verb is incomplete.

quests.question: Please be _____ when you discuss salaries; some details are confidential.
quests.explanation: "Discreet" means careful not to reveal private information. "Discrete" means separate and distinct, and is a common spelling mistake.

quests.question: Passengers for Flight 214 should _____ to Gate 12 for boarding.
quests.explanation: "Proceed" means to go forward, and airports use it in announcements. "Precede" means to come before something.

quests.question: Always _____ your sources in an academic essay.
quests.explanation: "Cite" means to mention a source as evidence, and it is pronounced like "site". The two words sound the same but have different meanings.

quests.question: I can't _____ the noise from the building site any longer.
quests.explanation: "Bear" as a verb means to tolerate something unpleasant. "Bare" is an adjective meaning uncovered.

quests.question: She _____ the documents on the desk and left the room.
quests.explanation: The verb "lay" needs an object, here "the documents", and its past form is "laid". "Lay" is the past of "lie" (to recline), so it is a common confusion.

quests.question: Open the window, _____?
quests.explanation: A tag question after an imperative uses "will you" or "would you" to soften the command. "Do you" and "did you" are used for different structures.

quests.question: You can reduce errors _____ checking each figure twice.
quests.explanation: We use "by" + -ing to say how something is achieved. It describes the method that leads to the result.

quests.question: She handled the complaint _____, and the customer left satisfied.
quests.explanation: The word describes how she handled the complaint, so an adverb is required. "Tactless" is an adjective with the opposite meaning.

quests.question: Three-quarters of the budget _____ already been spent.
quests.explanation: With fractions, the verb agrees with the noun that follows "of". "Budget" is singular, so we use "has"; compare "three-quarters of the staff have".
